name: Dice game
summary:
You are asked to participate in a game of dice. The croupier will roll a regular dice two times and if the product of the resulting pips is at least 19, you get a pay-off of 36€. The stake for the game is 9€.

When the croupier sees your hesitance to play, you are offered to see the result of the first die roll for 4€, before paying additional 6€ to continue to the second die roll.

What will you do to maximize your expected pay-off?

levels.name: Framing
levels.description:
To help the decision-making process we should be clear on the framing.

What can be considered as 'given', and is out of scope for the decision at hand?
What is to be decided 'out of scope' and not important for now?
What is actually the decision to take and is therefore 'in scope'?

levels.name: Decision tree
levels.description:
A decision tree visualizes options, scenarios and potential outcomes (costs, benefits, probabilities) to guide you to the best decision.

Take a look at the picture below. Every square represents a decision and every circle an uncertain event.

To start with, you have 3 options to choose from: Play with both dice, Roll first die, Don't play.

In the next pages, you will step-by-step add probabilities to the paths in the decision tree, and add the costs and pay-offs.

levels.name: Decision tree - Select best decision (1)
levels.description:
To determine the best decision, you can calculate the expected value after each decision.

In case you choose to 'Play' the expected value is -1€ (= 0.222 * 36€ + 0.778 * 0€ - 9€). If you 'Don't Play' the expected value is 0€. Determine the other expected values.

questions.question: What is the expected value v1 if you stop after the first die roll?
questions.hint: You don't win anything in these cases, only play for the first die.

questions.question: What is the expected value v2 if you stop after the first die roll?
questions.hint: There is no chance of winning, only cost of playing.

questions.question: What is the expected value v3 if you stop after the first die roll?
questions.hint: Multiply the chance of winning with the pay-off, and substract the cost of playing.

questions.question: What is the expected value v3 if you stop after the first die roll?
questions.hint: Multiply the chance of winning with the pay-off, and substract the cost of playing.

questions.question: What is the expected value v5 if you decide to show the first die roll.
questions.hint: Remember that you will always choose the best option when shown the second die. Multipy the probabilities with that best option.
